mlb.abs_challenge_regime.label: ABS challenge-system zone regime (2026+): effective zone, challenge availability and success, catcher/batter challenge skill
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.measurement: From 2026 pitch-level data compute for each pitcher-catcher pair (a) share of borderline pitches (within 1.5 inches of the zone edge) called strikes after challenges, (b) challenge rate and overturn rate when the battery or the batter challenges, shrunk to league with k = 30 challenges, (c) the 2026 league difference in called-strike rate on edge pitches versus 2025. Replace umpire_k_bb_effect and framing priors with 2025-weighted estimates multiplied by the 2026 edge-pitch shrink factor (ratio of 2026 to 2025 edge called-strike variance across umpires). Units: change in K probability per batter. As-of: through prior games; 2026 data accumulate during the season.
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.mechanism: With automated ball-strike challenges, a borderline pitch can be overturned to the true zone, so called-strike probability on edge pitches, framing value and umpire zone effects shrink toward the robotic zone and challenge skill matters.
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.rationale: Every 2026 regular-season and postseason game (including the sampled Oct 28 2026 game) uses challenges (two per team, successful ones retained, extra challenges in extras), so strikeout-looking events, count leverage and framing value differ from the human-umpire seasons that supply most history; umpire and framing effects estimated on 2021-2025 do not transfer unchanged.

Units: pitches per PA and walk probability. As-of: through prior games; 2026 sample builds over the season.
mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.mechanism: Under automated ball-strike challenges the called zone on borderline pitches is more consistent, shifting walks, called strikes and therefore pitch cost per out relative to the human-umpire seasons that supply history.
mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.rationale: Pitches per PA is a history-based average and cannot contain the day's zone regime; all 2026 games use ABS challenges, which changes walks and called strikes. The pitch budget that caps outs depends on pitches per out, so an unmodelled regime shift mis-states the ceiling.

mlb.all_star_game_event_model.label: All-Star Game result and MVP model: league talent, exhibition usage and MVP credit given the winning team
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.measurement: P(league wins) from the difference in selected-roster strength (summed projected wOBA/ERA by lineup and pitching slots) mapped through the game-win logistic with a compressed slope (about 0.5 of the regular-season slope, to be estimated from 2010-2025 results). P(MVP = player) = P(his league wins) x share, share = softmax of expected plate appearances x per-PA highlight probability (HR, multi-hit) with a pitcher-specific term for the winning pitcher. As-of: roster announcement and starting lineups.
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.mechanism: The exhibition has equal-stakes, short-stint pitcher usage and substitution rules, so the result is close to a coin flip and the MVP comes from the winning team's players with the most plate appearances and highlights.
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.rationale: KXMLBASGAME and KXMLBASGMVP resolve on a one-off game: league strength differences are tiny relative to variance, and MVP depends on the winning side, plate appearances and extra-base or home-run events.

mlb.all_star_selection_model.label: All-Star selection model: fan-vote phases, player vote, commissioner/roster-fill rules and positional slots
mlb.all_star_selection_model.measurement: P(selected) = P(starter via fan vote) + P(reserve via player vote | not starter) + P(added by commissioner or as replacement | neither). Fan-vote share modelled from last-year vote share, WAR rank at the ballot-close date and market size with a multinomial logit by position (shrinkage k = 2 seasons); player-vote probability from WAR rank within position; team-representation fill from the rule that each club has at least one selectee. Calibrate on 2015-2025 selections. As-of: ballot phase timestamps.
mlb.all_star_selection_model.mechanism: A player is selected through fan voting that fixes starters, a player vote and then commissioner or roster-fill picks, so selection probability depends on vote share, position slot and team-representation rules.
mlb.all_star_selection_model.rationale: KXMLBALLSTAR cannot be modelled from season production alone: starters are fan-determined, reserves player-chosen and pitchers and replacements follow rules, with injured selectees replaced and each team is assured a representative.

mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.label: All-Star Game format and tiebreak regime for the year (innings, extra-inning or swing-off rule, pitcher limits)
mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.measurement: Record per year: scheduled innings, extra-inning rule (automatic runner or not), tiebreak mechanism if any, pitch-count or innings limits, DH use in both leagues, roster size. Encode as categorical regime flags; reweight historical games by regime similarity (weight 1 for same regime, 0.4 otherwise). Collect the commissioner's announcement of rule changes before the event and flag any change announced after market open. P(tie after 9) taken from 14 years of scores as a prior around 0.05-0.10, to be checked.

mlb.asg_format_tiebreak_rules.rationale: Since 2022 (first actually used in 2025) a game tied after nine innings goes to a swing-off (three hitters per side) instead of extra innings, and earlier years used automatic-runner extras; the 2026 rules text confirms a swing-off can end the game. A swing-off decision changes credit because swing-off events are visible but may not count as game statistics.

For the target year use the posted rosters, listed starters and probable pitchers as of the market timestamp; refresh at lineup announcement (about 1-2 hours before first pitch). Output per player: P(any PA), PA distribution over {0,1,2,3,4}; per pitcher: P(pitches), expected BF.
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.mechanism: Each hitter's plate appearances and each pitcher's batters faced in the exhibition are set by roster composition, the two managers' substitution habits and the announced pitching order, not by a season-long role.
mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan.rationale: A player who is named but enters in the 6th inning gets one or two PAs; a starter gets two or three. Pitchers are normally used for one inning each, so strikeouts come from many arms facing a few batters. Withdrawn players are replaced by commissioner picks, which changes both pool and slots. Every per-player ASG market is first a participation question.

mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.label: Joint distribution of award outcomes for combination markets
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.measurement: Estimate pairwise dependence between award outcomes by a Gaussian copula fitted to 25 seasons of winners (same-team indicator, shared-electorate indicator) shrunk to independence with k = 10 seasons; P(A and B) = C(P(A), P(B); rho). Units: probability. As-of: after finalists are announced.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.mechanism: A combination market pays only if several awards go to specified outcomes, whose probabilities are correlated through shared player performance and team narrative.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.rationale: KXMLBAWARDCOMBO needs P(A and B), not the product: an MVP and Cy Young from the same team are positively dependent via team success, while two MVPs in different leagues are nearly independent; the electorates also differ.

mlb.award_vote_rank_model.label: Rank-ordered voter model (Plackett-Luce) for award points and finalists
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.measurement: Fit Plackett-Luce on 15 seasons of MVP/Cy Young/ROY ballot results: utility_i = b1*WAR_z + b2*team_success + b3*counting_stat_z + b4*narrative_flag + position effects; voter-level noise variance estimated from vote dispersion; shrink coefficients across awards with k = 3 seasons. For finalist market compute P(rank <= 3) by simulation with voter noise. As-of: ballot deadline stats plus narrative flags. Units: probabilities.
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.mechanism: Awards are decided by ballots ranking candidates; the distribution over rankings, not a single score, gives winner and finalist probabilities.
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.rationale: A winner market and a finalist market need different parts of the same ranking distribution; point totals depend on ballot structure (first-place votes, 10-deep ballots) and on how the voters weigh WAR, counting stats and team success.

mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.label: Run-expectancy conversion of baserunners (RE24-allowed by base-out state, pitcher profile)
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.measurement: For each pitcher over 2 seasons (half-life 400 BF): runs per baserunner = (runs allowed charged) / (H + BB + HBP); decompose with RE24 table: for each PA, delta RE given outcome. Fit pitcher-specific outcome probabilities by base-out state (K with runners on, GB with runner on first, HR/FB), shrink to league with k = 250 BF. Expected ER for the lineup = sum over PAs from a Markov simulation using these state-dependent outcomes and the confirmed batting order; subtract expected unearned share (see er_ur_scoring_split). Units: runs per 9 innings equivalent, then per BF. As-of: lineup post.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.mechanism: Earned runs equal the sum of run-value increments across base-out states; HR and extra-base hits convert traffic to runs.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.rationale: LOB% regression treats strand rate as luck, but strand rate partly reflects pitcher skill (K and GB with runners on) and HR timing. A direct PA-level run-expectancy accounting separates how many baserunners a pitcher allows from how many each is worth.
raw_data: event-level: base-out state before, events, runs scored on play, batter, pitcher, park

mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.label: Batted-ball outcome model P(1B, 2B, 3B, HR | exit velocity, launch angle, spray, park, defense)
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.measurement: Fit a multinomial model on 4 seasons of batted-ball events: outcome ~ spline(launch_speed, launch_angle) x spray_angle x park (random effect) x batter hand x fielder alignment indicator (post-2023 shift limits). For each hitter compute his batted-ball distribution (EV, LA, spray) over 2 seasons half-life 200 BIP with shrinkage to hand-class k = 150 BIP, then expected outcome mix for the game park. Expected TB per PA = P(K)=0 + sum outcome probability x bases; units bases per PA. As-of: lineup post.
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.mechanism: Total bases weights outcomes 1-4, so per-hit and per-PA probabilities of each outcome type, not just hit probability, drive TB rungs.
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.rationale: xBA and xSLG are season-aggregate and park-neutral; a single game needs the outcome mix given the actual park, handedness and the opposing defense. Doubles and triples depend on spray and park geometry (gap depth, wall height) and on runner speed, and HR depends on the carry.

mlb.battery_assignment.label: Pitcher-catcher battery effect (actual catcher assigned) on K%-over-expected
mlb.battery_assignment.measurement: For each pitcher-catcher pair over 3 seasons: K%-over-expected = (K - sum p_i)/BF using the matchup-model expectation excluding the catcher; shrink the pair effect to the catcher's overall framing runs per 1000 called pitches with k = 250 BF. Pre-lineup: P(catcher = c) from the team's rotation of catchers conditioned on rest pattern; post-lineup: realised catcher. Units: K probability points per BF. As-of: lineup post timestamp.
mlb.battery_assignment.mechanism: The catcher selected for the start changes framing, pitch-calling and blocking; some pitchers have personal catchers.
mlb.battery_assignment.rationale: Existing catcher_framing is a team-season catcher metric; what moves a single start is which catcher is in the lineup card and whether the pitcher is paired with him. Backup catchers have a materially different framing level and often start day games after night games, so it is partly predictable from the schedule.

mlb.batting_behind_protection.label: Quality of the hitters batting behind (on-deck and following) as a pitch-around and intentional-walk driver
mlb.batting_behind_protection.measurement: For hitter h in slot s of the confirmed lineup, compute protection = mean projected wOBA (vs the starter's hand, shrunk to ZiPS/Steamer with k = 300 PA) of the next two hitters in the order, minus the league mean wOBA, in wOBA points. Convert to expected intentional-plus-unintentional walk-rate shift using a regression of BB% on protection with first-base-open flag over 2021-2025 (shrunk by hitter with k = 200 PA). Output: change in per-PA walk probability and in the P(runner goes) at first base. As-of: lineup post.
mlb.batting_behind_protection.mechanism: Pitchers and managers decide whether to pitch to or around a hitter, and whether to hold or send a runner, based on who follows; a weak hitter on deck raises walks and intentional walks for the current hitter and lowers his RBI chances.
mlb.batting_behind_protection.rationale: RBI conversion and steal attempts both depend on the batter behind: with first base open a dangerous on-deck hitter lowers the walk rate, while a weak one invites intentional walks that remove RBI chances. This is stated only in interactions today and has no measurable input; it also changes the green light for a runner on first.

mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.label: Bonus-pool and slot-value structure: assigned slot values per pick, club pool size, overage tax and forfeiture thresholds, and incentives for underslot top picks
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.measurement: Official slot values for picks 1-75 and each club's total pool for the draft year; per club compute (pool total, number of picks in the top 75, share of pool in its first pick). Historical below-slot discount at slots 1-10: (bonus minus slot)/slot by club and class, 2012-2025. Output a per-club underslot propensity score in [0,1].
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.mechanism: Clubs maximise total draft value under a hard-ish bonus pool, so taking a cheaper player at a high slot frees money for later picks.
mlb.bonus_pool_slot_strategy.rationale: Exceeding the pool by up to 5% costs a 75% tax and larger overages cost future first-round picks, so pools act as a budget constraint. Clubs with several early picks or a deep later class have strong incentives to sign the slot-5 pick below value, which favours college seniors and players with low leverage over the consensus talent.

mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.label: Probability the home team's bottom of the ninth is skipped (home lead after 8.5) and its run-total effect
mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.measurement: P(skip) = P(home leads after 8.5 innings) from the run distribution: P(home leads after top of 9) computed by convolving inning-level scores through 8 innings plus the visitors' top-9 distribution. Expected truncation loss in total = P(skip) x E[home runs in a bottom-9 inning] (about 0.5 runs). Adjust the mean total by that amount and widen the lower tail. As-of: lineup post with projected win probability. Units: runs of expected truncation. WALK-OFF TRUNCATION: when the home team trails or is tied entering the bottom of the 9th (or an extra inning), the half-inning ends once it takes the lead, so remaining runs are lost; compute the home team's expected runs in that half under the stopping rule (capped at runs needed plus the homer exception) and apply the loss separately to the home team total (KXMLBTEAMTOTAL for the home side), which is truncated, versus the visitor total, which is not, and to the combined game total.
mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.mechanism: A home team ahead after the top of the ninth does not bat, so its runs and the game total are truncated relative to nine full innings.
mlb.bottom_ninth_truncation.rationale: A total of 8.5 is often priced as if both teams bat nine innings; in games where the home team is ahead the home runs stop early, shifting probability toward under, and the truncation is correlated with favorite status and low total.
raw_data: linescore: runs by inning by team, innings played, home flag

mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.label: Postseason bracket-path enumeration: pairing, series length and home-field pattern probabilities
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.measurement: Enumerate all bracket paths from the current seeds or seed probabilities: P(path) = product of series-win probabilities from the team-strength posterior; series length distribution from per-game probabilities with home-field pattern (2-3-2 or 2-2-1-1-1) and shared team-strength draws; games hosted = sum over series of the home games in the realised length. Output P(matchup A vs B in round r) and the distribution of games hosted by a team. As-of: daily.
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.mechanism: Matchup, games-hosted and qualifier contracts are functions of which teams reach which round and how long each series lasts.
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.rationale: KXMLBMATCHUP and KXMLBPLAYOFFHOST resolve on bracket pairing and on how many games each team hosts, which requires enumerating the fixed bracket (no reseeding within the 12-team format, to be verified) with series-length distributions and home-field patterns, not a title-probability number.

mlb.broadcast_airtime_distribution.label: Broadcast airtime distribution (game duration with delay and extras scenarios, plus included pre/post segments)
mlb.broadcast_airtime_distribution.measurement: Simulate duration = base minutes (team pair mean time per game, 2023+ pitch-clock regime, half-life 60 games) + 17 minutes x extra innings + delay minutes with probability from delay_risk; shift for pre-game and post-game windows if counted. Output distribution of exposure hours. Shrink team-pair means to league with k = 25 games. As-of: lineup post. Units: hours.
mlb.broadcast_airtime_distribution.mechanism: Exposure is the time on air, a random variable depending on pace, extras, delays and scheduling.
mlb.broadcast_airtime_distribution.rationale: The mention count scales with airtime, but airtime is uncertain: from a pitch-clock game of 2h25m to a 4h delayed extra-inning game, and pre/post segments may be inside or outside the contract window.

mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.label: Calendar hazard function by transaction type (trade, free-agent signing, extension, manager hire)
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.measurement: From 15 years of transactions: daily event counts per type normalized by eligible stock; fit a piecewise log-linear hazard with calendar-anchor dummies (deadline week, winter meetings week, non-tender day, spring training start). Output h(d) for the window dates and survival to the end. Shrink per-type to pooled with k = 3 seasons. Units: events per eligible per day. As-of: current stock of eligible players.
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.mechanism: Hazard of each event type is concentrated on known dates.
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.rationale: Using a flat per-day rate misprices markets that straddle deadlines and meeting dates; for example, a large share of free-agent signings occur in specific off-season windows and trade completions spike near the deadline.

As-of: public reports timestamped before the snapshot; discount single-source leaks to weight 0.5 until confirmed by a second outlet.

mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.label: Bargaining calendar hazard: days to expiry, owners' lockout decision date, spring-training and scheduled-opener deadlines
mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.measurement: Build a discrete-time hazard on weekly steps from expiry to the scheduled opener plus 60 days: h(t) = P(agreement in week t | none yet), with features: weeks to the next hard deadline (spline), lockout in force flag, number of formal sessions in last 14 days, gap index. Fit on 1972, 1973, 1976, 1980-81, 1985, 1990, 1994-95, 2002, 2016 and 2021-22 episodes with strong shrinkage; map to P(first regular-season game before May 31) = P(agreement by the date implied by scheduled opening plus allowed ramp-up (about 3-4 weeks for spring training)). Dates taken from the published schedule and CBA text as of the snapshot.

mlb.cba_negotiation_timeline_hazard.rationale: The CBA expiry on December 1, 2026 is the first deadline; the second is the February pitchers-and-catchers report date; the third is the scheduled opener. The named pitcher's market is near zero if he is shut down; the any-pitcher market loses its tail contributors one by one.

mlb.home_field_run_advantage.rationale: A constant HFA hides park differences (dimensions, sightlines, altitude familiarity) and the structural last-at-bat advantage that produces extra home wins in tied late innings and truncates the bottom-9th when the home team leads.

As-of: pitcher announcement before the snapshot.
mlb.hr_derby_bp_pitcher_pairing.mechanism: Per-swing HR rate depends on how hittable and repeatable the batting-practice pitches are; each hitter picks his own pitcher (often a coach or relative), so the pitcher is a hitter-specific matchup input.

mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.label: Home Run Derby round output under the 2026 swing-capped format: swings allotted, per-swing HR rate, last-swing extension and advancement
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.measurement: Per hitter: p = P(HR | swing) estimated from season barrel rate, pulled fly-ball rate and max-EV percentile (through the day before the Derby) mapped to Derby HR per swing using 2015-2025 Derby swing logs (timed-format years, swing outcomes only, not volume), shrunk to the pooled Derby mean with k = 40 swings, adjusted by the BP-pitcher term and host-park carry. Round HR ~ Binomial(n_r, p) + extension E where E is geometric with P(last swing HR) x p/(1-p) expected extra homers; n_r = 20, 15, 15. Fatigue as a multiplicative decay on p per round (prior 0.97, shrunk). Simulate the pool, the longest-HR Round 1 tiebreak and three-swing swing-offs. As-of: field and rulebook at the snapshot.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.mechanism: With a fixed swing allotment (20 in Round 1, 15 in the semifinal and final) a round's homers equal the sum of per-swing HR indicators plus a geometric extension when the last allotted swing is a homer; the clock, pitcher pace and bonus time no longer exist.
mlb.hr_derby_bracket_throughput_model.rationale: Under swing caps volume is fixed, so the levers are per-swing HR rate, selectivity (takes appear not to count against the allotment, so waiting for a hittable pitch costs nothing but time) and the quality of the hitter's chosen batting-practice pitcher. Round 1 is an eight-man pool where the top four advance, so the advancement threshold depends on the whole field's rates, not on one opponent.

mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.label: Derby extremes: probability of 500+ foot homers, longest homer and peak exit velocity over the event
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.measurement: For each hitter fit a generalized Pareto tail to HR distances and exit velocities above his own 85th percentile over 3 seasons of Statcast (min 25 exceedances, else borrow league shape and use own scale shrunk with k = 15), plus a Derby uplift estimated from 2015-2025 Derby versus in-game tails. Number of draws per hitter = homers from the throughput model, i.e. 20 Round 1 swings, plus 15 more if he reaches the semifinal and 15 more in the final, plus extensions; this makes extremes depend on bracket advancement, not clock. Adjust for host-park carry from mlb.park_specific_xhr and weather. Simulate jointly with the throughput model because the Round 1 tie rule (longest HR) couples totals and distances; report P(any >= 525 ft), P(500+ count >= k), P(each hitter has longest), P(each hitter has highest EV HR). As-of: games through the previous day.
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.mechanism: Longest-HR, 500+ ft count and highest exit velocity are maxima of batted-ball distributions over a few hundred swings, so they live in the upper tail of each hitter's power distribution.
mlb.hr_derby_distance_ev_extreme.rationale: A batter's average HR distance says little about whether he reaches 500 or 525 ft. Tail behaviour needs top-decile EV and distance, park and wind carry, and the number of homers he gets, which under the 2026 format is set by rounds reached. Longest and highest-EV series are dead-heated at the league's reported precision, so rounding matters.

mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.label: Home Run Derby field: who is invited, who accepts, withdrawal and replacement hazard, seeding
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.measurement: For each year 2015-2025 record the invited list at announcement dates, acceptance, final eight, replacements and seeding rule. Model P(accept | rank in season HR, prior participation, age, team home park hosting, injury status) as a logistic with shrinkage k = 5 per feature group. As-of: use announcements dated before the market snapshot; late replacement flagged separately. Output: P(player in final eight) and the seed table.
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.mechanism: The Derby field is a self-selected set of hitters, so qualifier and winner markets depend on acceptance, injury withdrawals and replacement choices.
mlb.hr_derby_field_and_withdrawal.rationale: Top sluggers often decline, and replacements arrive days before the event (Murakami was the eighth and final addition in 2026 after returning from the injured list). The field is both an input and a target: KXMLBHRDERBYQUAL settles Yes on selection even if the player then withdraws, while every other Derby market resolves No for a non-participant. Round 1 in 2026 is pool play, so seeding no longer sets Round 1 opponents; semifinal pairings follow Round 1 rank.

mlb.hrfb_regression.mechanism: Home runs per fly ball regress strongly to a mean determined by park and contact quality, so past HR luck is not persistent.
mlb.hrfb_regression.rationale: HR markets and earned-run totals depend on HR/FB; a hot HR/FB streak revert. Subtle: for hitters with elite barrel rates, HR/FB is persistently high; park-adjust.

mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.label: Impasse, implemented terms, replacement-player and labour-board/injunction state of the dispute
mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.measurement: Track as an ordinal state with dates: 0 bargaining, 1 lockout or strike, 2 impasse declared or terms implemented, 3 replacement players signed or scheduled, 4 ULP charge filed, 5 NLRB complaint or 10(j) petition, 6 injunction granted or denied. Hazard of season start = baseline from the bargaining hazard plus a state-specific term (state 6 granted implies return within about 3 weeks, from 1995). Sources timestamped; NLRB docket entries verified by case number. As-of: filings and announcements before the snapshot.
mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.mechanism: A stoppage can end without agreement: owners may declare bargaining impasse and implement terms or field replacement players, and the union may file unfair-labour-practice charges leading to an NLRB complaint and a federal injunction that restores prior terms and returns players.
mlb.impasse_replacement_legal_state.rationale: The 1994-95 strike ended when the NLRB obtained a federal injunction (March 31, 1995) restoring the expired terms, after owners had used replacement players in spring training. This route changes both timing and what counts: replacement-player games could be official regular-season games, and an injunction can start a season without a new CBA.

mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.label: Inherited-runner charge risk after starter exit (expected extra earned runs)
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.measurement: P(exit with k runners) from the hazard model (see leash) x P(each inherited runner scores | reliever profile) with reliever strand rate shrunk to league (k = 60 BF with inherited runners). Expected extra ER = sum_k P(k) x k x p_score x (1-unearned share). Use the likely first reliever from bullpen availability (setup man or long man). Units: expected earned runs added. As-of: lineup post + bullpen usage from prior 2 days.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.mechanism: A starter is charged for runners left on base when relieved, so the bullpen strand rate determines part of his earned runs.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.rationale: The starter's earned-run count is not finished when he leaves: if he leaves with traffic and the reliever allows them to score, those runs are his. Exit-with-traffic probability is high in blow-up outings, the same outings that populate the right tail of the ER ladder.
raw_data: relief-appearance level: inherited runners, inherited scored, reliever, team, game state

mlb.inning_index_scoring_profile.label: Team scoring and allowed-runs profile by inning index (1st versus 2nd-8th)
mlb.inning_index_scoring_profile.measurement: Per team: runs per half-inning for innings 1, 2-3, 4-6, 7-9 over last 3 seasons, shrink to league-by-inning k = 100 half-innings. Use for baseline; for team-pair adjust multiplicatively by opponent (ratio to league). Units: runs per half-inning. As-of: prior game.
mlb.inning_index_scoring_profile.mechanism: Offence is stronger early (top of order due up) and weaker late (relievers, platoon-optimised matchups).
mlb.inning_index_scoring_profile.rationale: League scoring in the first inning exceeds other innings because the best hitters bat; team and park differences in first-inning versus other-inning scoring are mostly noise but have systematic pieces (starter quality, lineup top-heaviness).
raw_data: inning-level runs by team, park, home/away

mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.label: Joint season HR-SB distribution for one hitter (power-speed profile, PA, availability)
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.measurement: Given current HR, SB and remaining games: HR_rest ~ NB with mean = rate_HR * PA_rest, SB_rest ~ NB with mean = rate_SB * PA_rest x opportunity; PA_rest from games remaining x P(play) x PA per game; correlation via shared PA factor and a latent role; compute P(HR >= 50 and SB >= 40) by simulation. Rates from rest-of-season projection blended with current-season pace (shrunk k = 250 PA). Units: probability. As-of: daily.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.mechanism: A 50 HR and 40 SB season is a joint tail of two correlated counts requiring health and PA.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.rationale: The probability depends on the hitter's season-to-date pace, remaining PA and the rates of both events, and the two are correlated through playing time and hitter quality; independence misprices.
raw_data: player daily stats; ROS projections; sprint speed; injury status

mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.label: Labour-stoppage regime: CBA expiry (Dec 1 2026), lockout flag and expected end, and transaction freeze rules
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.measurement: State variables: days to CBA expiry, lockout flag, days since lockout start, reported negotiation status (own capture of timestamped reports coded into ordinal stage 0-4). Model the stoppage length L with a survival model whose prior is built from the 1994-95, 2021-22 and 1990 stoppages (3 events, heavy shrinkage) and updated by negotiation stage; apply the freeze: hazard of any 40-man transaction = 0 during lockout, with a post-agreement rush multiple estimated from March 2022 (units: multiple of baseline hazard). Output P(freeze covers date d) and the adjusted calendar hazard. As-of: daily.
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.mechanism: A lockout freezes 40-man roster transactions and free-agent signings, turning a window into a pre-expiry rush, a frozen interval of unknown length and a post-deal rush.
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.rationale: The 2022 CBA expires at 11:59 pm ET on Dec 1 2026 and a lockout is widely reported as likely; in 2021-22 the lockout froze 40-man transactions from Dec 2 until Mar 10 2022. A next-team market closing Mar 25 2027 and any call-up or opening-day contract in 2027 are therefore mixtures over stoppage length, and 15 years of calendar hazard history include only one such stoppage.
raw_data: CBA expiry date and labour news timeline
transactions log around 1990, 1994-95 and 2021-22

mlb.late_inning_leverage_deployment.label: Reliever deployment by lead size (who pitches innings 7-9 as a function of margin) and its run-prevention effect
mlb.late_inning_leverage_deployment.measurement: For each team over the last 2 seasons: runs allowed per inning in innings 7-9 by lead bucket (tie/within1, 2-3, 4+) and by reliever tier (top-3 by leverage index vs rest). Shrink bucket runs allowed to league with k = 100 innings. Combine with the margin distribution through a Markov simulation in innings 7-9: P(margin change | state). Units: run-allowed rate by state. As-of: bullpen availability at lineup post.
mlb.late_inning_leverage_deployment.mechanism: Managers use high-leverage relievers in close games and low-leverage arms in blowouts, compressing and lumpifying the margin.
mlb.late_inning_leverage_deployment.rationale: A margin spread cover is not a symmetric diffusion: leads of one to three runs are protected by the best bullpen arms while four-plus leads are mopped up by weaker arms, so favorites win by exactly one or two more often than a normal model suggests.
raw_data: inning-level: team, inning, score diff, pitcher used, leverage index, runs allowed

mlb.late_replacement_risk.label: Early-removal and pinch-hit-for risk for a starting hitter (PA truncation)

Shrink hitter rate to role-class (everyday, platoon, catcher, veteran DH) with k = 60 games. Output vector of survival probabilities to PA3, PA4, PA5. As-of: confirmed lineup + pregame total.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.mechanism: A starter may be lifted for a pinch hitter or defensive replacement, so PA count is truncated and the late PAs against the bullpen go to someone else.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.rationale: Slot-based PA expectations assume a full game; platoon players, catchers and aging regulars are routinely removed in high-leverage late innings or in blowouts, and the settlement counts only the starter's own PAs.
raw_data: game-level: batter, slot, PA count, replaced_by, replaced_inning, score at replacement, opposing reliever hand

mlb.late_scratch_hazard.label: Late-scratch hazard between lineup posting and first pitch (conditional on listed starter)

The 1-3% base rate and any start probabilities in the stage text (0.9, 0.3-0.7, 0.1) are illustrative author priors, not fitted values. mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.label: Lightning-proximity exposure within the league's 8-mile safety radius over the game window
mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.measurement: From a lightning-strike archive (GOES-R GLM or NLDN), compute historical frequency of strikes within 8 miles of the park during the 3.5-hour window by month and local-hour; combine with the forecast CAPE/convective probability from the forecast vintage via logistic regression calibrated on 5 seasons of recorded delays. Output P(lightning within 8 mi in game window). As-of: 3 hours before first pitch and update at lineup post. Units: probability. ASSUMPTION: the 8-mile radius and 30-minute hold are common convention (stadium or umpire discretion); MLB publishes no uniform league rule. GOES-R GLM gives optical flashes, not NLDN strikes, so archive-based frequencies are a proxy.
mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.mechanism: Lightning within a set radius triggers mandatory delays independent of rain amount.
mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure.rationale: A forecast of rain probability misses thunderstorms with sparse precipitation; lightning radius rules cause delays even when the field is dry, and conversely rain can come without lightning and be played through.
raw_data: strike timestamp and coordinates; park coordinates; forecast convective variables; recorded weather delays

mlb.lineup_strength_delta.label: Day-specific lineup strength delta (confirmed lineup vs team baseline, in runs per game)
mlb.lineup_strength_delta.measurement: delta (runs per game) = sum over slots s of PA_share(s) x (wOBA_proj(hitter_s, vs starter hand) - wOBA_proj(team regular at slot s)) / wOBA_scale, with wOBA_scale about 1.2 (so 0.100 team-wide wOBA over about 38 PA is about 3.2 runs); PA_share already sums to about 38.2 PA per game, so no further 9-inning multiplier is applied. Projections from rest-of-season systems (ZiPS/Steamer) blended with 2-season xwOBA shrunk to projection k = 300 PA. PA_share from slot PA expectations (4.65, 4.55, 4.45, 4.35, 4.25, 4.15, 4.05, 3.95, 3.85). Units: runs per game. As-of: lineup post.
mlb.lineup_strength_delta.mechanism: The nine hitters who actually play differ from the team's season baseline because of rest days, platoon choices and injuries.
mlb.lineup_strength_delta.rationale: Team-level wRC+ averages across the season's lineups; the confirmed card might lack its best hitter or contain a bench bat, and the effect is not uniform across the order (top slots get more PAs).
raw_data: lineup card (hitter, slot), projection table, handedness

mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.label: Lockout and shortened-season scenario: P(lockout), start/end dates and games lost under each scenario
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.measurement: Scenario mixture: P(no lockout) from negotiation state (own timestamped coding of reports, ordinal 0-4); conditional on a lockout, the stoppage end date drawn from a survival model with prior from 1990, 1994-95 and 2021-22 (3 events, strongly shrunk) updated by negotiation stage; games lost = schedule games before the agreed start date after a compressed ramp-up (about 3 weeks of spring training), with doubleheaders making up part. Output: P(first regular-season game before May 31 2027) and P(games played > 600) = P(games lost < 1,830). As-of: daily.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.mechanism: A CBA lockout after Dec 1 2026 could delay opening day and cancel games, so season-games and opening-day outcomes are mixtures over scenarios.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.rationale: A 600-game strike equals roughly a quarter of the 2,430-game schedule and a May 31 opening cutoff is a long delay; both are plausible stoppage thresholds. In 2021-22 the lockout postponed opening day by about one week with no games lost (to my knowledge), but 1994-95 lost the end of one season and the start of the next; the distribution of games lost is heavy-tailed with a large mass at zero.

mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.label: Longest winning streak: extreme-value distribution given team win probabilities and remaining games

P(team has strict maximum) = Prod over rivals (1 - ...) with Monte Carlo and tie share 1/N (payout rounded down). Streak serial correlation assumed zero unless tested. As-of: daily. Units: probability. Postponed, suspended and cancelled games are excluded from the sequence; the streak model assumes independent games conditional on p_ij, so serial correlation and doubleheader order are assumptions.

mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.rationale: Season streak markets are filed in this archetype but are not inning markets; the winning team is the one with the longest run, with ties paying $1/N, so the exact distribution of the maximum run for each team (given per-game win probability, mostly 0.4-0.65) determines the odds.

mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.label: Manager/executive award score: wins over preseason expectation, division outcome and turnaround
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.measurement: score = (actual wins - preseason projected wins, ZiPS/PECOTA/consensus) + 3 x division title flag + 2 x playoff berth + 0.5 x improvement vs prior season wins (scaled), computed at the ballot deadline; map to vote probability by multinomial logit calibrated on 15 seasons of finalist votes (shrink k = 3 seasons). Executive award adds payroll efficiency and offseason acquisitions. Units: composite score and probability. As-of: at ballot deadline and updated daily.
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.mechanism: Awards for managers and executives are voted on surprise and success relative to expectation rather than on absolute record.
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.rationale: Votes correlate more with wins minus preseason projection (and a division title or big turnaround) than with wins alone; the voting ballot closes before the postseason, so late-season trajectory and awards-ballot deadline matter.

mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.label: Remaining exposure to max-effort fastballs: expected count of high-velocity fastballs per candidate over the rest of the season and postseason
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.measurement: Per candidate: projected remaining appearances (role, health) x fastballs per appearance x share of fastballs within 1.5 mph of his season max (from his own pitch-level data, last 60 days with shrinkage to prior season, k = 300 pitches); add postseason expected appearances = P(team reaches each round) x expected games x appearance rate. Units: expected near-peak fastballs. As-of: daily.
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.mechanism: The chance that the season maximum crosses a threshold rises with the number of near-peak attempts, so exposure is the volume term of the extreme.
mlb.max_effort_pitch_exposure.rationale: A closer throws perhaps 600-900 fastballs a year, nearly all at full effort; a starter throws more but paces, so only first-inning and high-leverage fastballs approach his ceiling. Exposure must count near-peak attempts, not all pitches, and must add postseason games only with the team's probability of playing them.
